$comment: Shapes, not behaviour -- and every field name here is taken from HubSpot's published OpenAPI document (SimplePublicObject), not from memory. The id is a NUMERIC STRING, which is the detail worth being faithful about: an author who wires it into a follow-up call and finds a number there in one runtime and a string in another has a bug that only appears across languages.

values.$comment: Drawn once, before the response. HubSpot returns the same id in two places -- `id` at the top and `hs_object_id` inside properties -- and two draws would produce a contact that cannot exist. An author who reads one and writes back the other would be testing against a shape the provider never sends.

response.$archivedComment: Never true. A faked contact that claimed to be archived would make the downstream guard -- act only on a live contact -- untestable, which is the branch most worth covering.
